guide.title: The Camino Francés from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Santiago de Compostela
guide.author: friends of Placemoir
guide.summary: The classic 780 km pilgrim route across northern Spain in 33 stages, from the Pyrenees over the meseta to Galicia, with a place to sleep at the end of each day and the sights and meals worth stopping for.

places.name: Accueil des Pèlerins
places.address: 39 Rue de la Citadelle, 64220 Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, France
places.notes: The volunteer pilgrim office on the cobbled main street. Pick up a credential and the first stamp, and ask about conditions on the Route Napoléon before setting out, since the high pass can close in bad weather.
places.section: Stage 1 · Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Roncesvalles · 25 km

places.name: Refuge Orisson
places.address: RD 428, 64220 Uhart-Cize
places.notes: A mountain refuge about 8 km up the climb, for those who want to split the Pyrenees crossing in two. Shared dinner on a terrace with a long view back over the valley. Open roughly April to mid-October; check the official site for booking.
places.section: Stage 1 · Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Roncesvalles · 25 km

places.name: Albergue de Roncesvalles
places.address: Calle Única s/n, 31650 Roncesvalles, Navarra
places.notes: The big pilgrim hostel in the restored monastery buildings, run by the Colegiata. Bunks are in tidy cubicles and nearly everyone starting in Saint-Jean sleeps here the first night.
places.section: Stage 1 · Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Roncesvalles · 25 km

places.name: Real Colegiata de Santa María de Roncesvalles
places.address: Calle Única s/n, 31650 Roncesvalles, Navarra
places.notes: A Gothic church and cloister that have sheltered pilgrims for about nine centuries. The evening pilgrim Mass with a blessing in several languages is a good way to end the first day.
places.section: Stage 1 · Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Roncesvalles · 25 km

places.name: Hostal Burguete
places.address: Calle de San Nikolas, 71, 31640 Auritz, Navarra
places.notes: An old family inn on the main street of Burguete, 3 km past Roncesvalles, where Hemingway stayed in the 1920s and wrote it into The Sun Also Rises. A comfortable private room after the first night in a dorm.
places.section: Stage 2 · Roncesvalles to Zubiri · 22 km

places.name: Puente de la Rabia
places.address: Calle del Puente de la Rabia, 31630 Esteribar, Navarra
places.notes: The medieval bridge over the Arga that leads into Zubiri. Local lore said walking an animal around its central pillar cured rabies. Most pilgrims cool their feet in the river below.
places.section: Stage 2 · Roncesvalles to Zubiri · 22 km

places.name: Albergue Jesús y María
places.address: Calle Compañía 4, 31001 Pamplona, Navarra
places.notes: The municipal pilgrim hostel inside a former Jesuit church in the old town, a few steps from the cathedral. Big, well run and central. It can close for stretches of the year, notably around San Fermín in July, so check before you go.
places.section: Stage 3 · Zubiri to Pamplona · 21 km

places.name: Café Iruña
places.address: Plaza del Castillo 44, 31001 Pamplona, Navarra
places.notes: A grand 1888 café on Plaza del Castillo with mirrors, marble and a long bar. Stop for coffee or pintxos and look for the Hemingway statue in the side room.
places.section: Stage 3 · Zubiri to Pamplona · 21 km

places.name: Catedral de Pamplona
places.address: Calle Dormitalería 1, 31001 Pamplona, Navarra
places.notes: Behind a neoclassical front is a Gothic church with one of the finest cloisters in Spain. The visit includes the old kitchen and a museum of Navarrese religious art.
places.section: Stage 3 · Zubiri to Pamplona · 21 km

places.name: Alto del Perdón
places.address: Calle San Andrés, 12, 31190 Zariquiegui, Navarra
places.notes: The windmill ridge about 13 km out of Pamplona, where iron silhouettes of medieval pilgrims on foot and horseback line the crest. Take the descent slowly; the loose stones are hard on knees.
places.section: Stage 4 · Pamplona to Puente la Reina · 24 km

places.name: Santa María de Eunate
places.address: Carretera NA-601 s/n, 31152 Muruzábal, Navarra
places.notes: An octagonal Romanesque church alone in the fields, ringed by an arcade. It is a short detour off the main route before Obanos; ask locally whether it is open before you go.
places.section: Stage 4 · Pamplona to Puente la Reina · 24 km

places.name: Albergue Padres Reparadores
places.address: Calle Crucifijo 1, 31100 Puente la Reina, Navarra
places.notes: A parish-style hostel run by a religious order at the entrance to town, beside the Church of the Crucifix. A garden out back for drying laundry and resting feet.
places.section: Stage 4 · Pamplona to Puente la Reina · 24 km

places.name: Puente Románico de Puente la Reina
places.address: Calle Mayor, 31100 Puente la Reina, Navarra
places.notes: The six-arched 11th-century bridge built for pilgrims over the Arga, at the end of the long main street. Cross it at dusk, then look back from the riverbank.
places.section: Stage 4 · Pamplona to Puente la Reina · 24 km

places.name: Iglesia de San Pedro de la Rúa
places.address: Calle San Pedro de la Rúa, 31200 Estella, Navarra
places.notes: A Romanesque church up a long stair above the Rúa, with a carved doorway and a partly surviving cloister. Visits are often by guided tour from the tourist office.
places.section: Stage 5 · Puente la Reina to Estella · 22 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal de Peregrinos de Estella
places.address: Calle La Rúa 50, 31200 Estella, Navarra
places.notes: The public hostel on the old pilgrim street, right on the route as you come into town and close to San Pedro de la Rúa.
places.section: Stage 5 · Puente la Reina to Estella · 22 km

places.name: Fuente del Vino de Irache
places.address: Camino de Santiago, 31240 Ayegui, Navarra
places.notes: A winery's free wine tap set into a wall beside the trail just past Estella, with a water tap next to it. A small glass is the custom, not a bottle refill.
places.section: Stage 6 · Estella to Los Arcos · 21 km

places.name: Iglesia de Santa María de Los Arcos
places.address: Plaza Santa María, 31210 Los Arcos, Navarra
places.notes: A plain outside hides a lavish Baroque interior and a quiet Gothic cloister. Many pilgrims time their evening around the Mass and blessing.
places.section: Stage 6 · Estella to Los Arcos · 21 km

places.name: Albergue Isaac Santiago
places.address: Calle San Lázaro s/n, 31210 Los Arcos, Navarra
places.notes: The municipal hostel at the far edge of Los Arcos, run by volunteers. A walled patio for stretching out after the long, dry walk from Villamayor.
places.section: Stage 6 · Estella to Los Arcos · 21 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal de Peregrinos de Logroño
places.address: Rúa Vieja 32, 26001 Logroño, La Rioja
places.notes: The city's public hostel in the old quarter, a short walk from the tapas streets. A shaded courtyard and plenty of beds.
places.section: Stage 7 · Los Arcos to Logroño · 28 km

places.name: Calle del Laurel
places.address: Calle del Laurel, 26001 Logroño, La Rioja
places.notes: A narrow old-town street packed with small bars, each known for one pincho, from grilled mushrooms to fried peppers, with a glass of Rioja. Go bar to bar rather than settling in one.
places.section: Stage 7 · Los Arcos to Logroño · 28 km

places.name: Iglesia de la Asunción de Navarrete
places.address: Calle La Cuesta, 26370 Navarrete, La Rioja
places.notes: A 16th-century church with an enormous gilded Baroque altarpiece, in a hill town known for pottery. A good rest stop about 12 km into the day.
places.section: Stage 8 · Logroño to Nájera · 29 km

places.name: Monasterio de Santa María la Real
places.address: Plaza Santa María 1, 26300 Nájera, La Rioja
places.notes: Built into the red cliff at the edge of town, with royal tombs of Navarre, a carved choir and a lacy Gothic cloister. The cave where the church was founded is at the back.
places.section: Stage 8 · Logroño to Nájera · 29 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal de Nájera
places.address: Plaza de Santiago s/n, 26300 Nájera, La Rioja
places.notes: A large public hostel run by volunteers just across the river in the old town, steps from the monastery.
places.section: Stage 8 · Logroño to Nájera · 29 km

places.name: Catedral de Santo Domingo de la Calzada
places.address: Plaza del Santo 4, 26250 Santo Domingo de la Calzada, La Rioja
places.notes: A live rooster and hen are kept in an ornate coop inside the cathedral, recalling the legend of the hanged pilgrim. Tradition says it is good luck if the rooster crows while you are inside.
places.section: Stage 9 · Nájera to Santo Domingo de la Calzada · 21 km

places.name: Parador de Santo Domingo de la Calzada
places.address: Plaza del Santo 3, 26250 Santo Domingo de la Calzada, La Rioja
places.notes: A state-run hotel in the medieval pilgrim hospital founded by the saint himself, facing the cathedral. Stone arches in the lobby and a quiet night if you want a break from bunks.
places.section: Stage 9 · Nájera to Santo Domingo de la Calzada · 21 km

places.name: Albergue Casa del Santo
places.address: Calle Mayor 42, 26250 Santo Domingo de la Calzada, La Rioja
places.notes: The confraternity's hostel on the main street, with a big kitchen and a yard where some of the cathedral's chickens are kept between shifts.
places.section: Stage 9 · Nájera to Santo Domingo de la Calzada · 21 km

places.name: Albergue Parroquial San Juan Bautista
places.address: Plaza de la Iglesia, 26259 Grañón, La Rioja
places.notes: Pilgrims sleep on mats in the loft of the parish church, cook and eat together, and pay by donation. No reservations. A night many remember long after the walk.
places.section: Stage 10 · Santo Domingo de la Calzada to Belorado · 23 km

places.name: Albergue Cuatro Cantones
places.address: Calle Hipólito López Bernal 10, 09250 Belorado, Burgos
places.notes: A family-run private hostel on the way into Belorado with a pool, a garden and a dining room serving pilgrim dinners.
places.section: Stage 10 · Santo Domingo de la Calzada to Belorado · 23 km

places.name: Hotel San Antón Abad
places.address: Calle Hospital 4, 09257 Villafranca Montes de Oca, Burgos
places.notes: A hotel in a 14th-century pilgrim hospital at the foot of the Oca hills, with private rooms and a separate pilgrim dorm. A good place to rest or stop for the night before the climb through the oak and pine forest.
places.section: Stage 11 · Belorado to San Juan de Ortega · 24 km

places.name: Monasterio de San Juan de Ortega
places.address: Calle de la Iglesia, 09199 San Juan de Ortega, Burgos
places.notes: A monastery church in a clearing in the oak forest, with the saint's tomb and a capital lit by the sun at the equinoxes. The pilgrim hostel is in the old monastery buildings next door.
places.section: Stage 11 · Belorado to San Juan de Ortega · 24 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal Casa del Cubo
places.address: Calle Fernán González 28, 09003 Burgos
places.notes: The city's public hostel in a restored town house right behind the cathedral. Large, modern and as central as it gets.
places.section: Stage 12 · San Juan de Ortega to Burgos · 26 km

places.name: Catedral de Burgos
places.address: Plaza de Santa María, 09003 Burgos
places.notes: One of the great Gothic cathedrals of Europe, with spires that look like stone lace and chapels that could each fill an afternoon. Pilgrims with a credential can ask about a reduced ticket.
places.section: Stage 12 · San Juan de Ortega to Burgos · 26 km

places.name: Cervecería Morito
places.address: Calle Diego Porcelos 1, 09003 Burgos
places.notes: A crowded tapas bar near the cathedral, known for generous plates of morcilla, croquetas and grilled mushrooms. Expect to wait for a spot at the bar.
places.section: Stage 12 · San Juan de Ortega to Burgos · 26 km

places.name: Ermita de Nuestra Señora de Monasterio
places.address: Camino de Santiago, 09130 Rabé de las Calzadas, Burgos
places.notes: A small chapel at the end of Rabé where a local woman has long offered pilgrims a blessing and a medal. The open meseta begins just beyond.
places.section: Stage 13 · Burgos to Hornillos del Camino · 21 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal de Hornillos del Camino
places.address: Plaza de la Iglesia s/n, 09230 Hornillos del Camino, Burgos
places.notes: A small public hostel beside the church in a one-street village on the meseta. Fills early, so carry on to the private hostels in the same street if it is full.
places.section: Stage 13 · Burgos to Hornillos del Camino · 21 km

places.name: Ruinas del Convento de San Antón
places.address: Carretera BU-P-4013, 09110 Castrojeriz, Burgos
places.notes: The road runs straight under the Gothic arches of a ruined 14th-century monastery, once a hospital for pilgrims. Volunteers run a simple candlelit hostel inside in the warmer months.
places.section: Stage 14 · Hornillos del Camino to Castrojeriz · 20 km

places.name: Castillo de Castrojeriz
places.address: Subida al Castillo, 09110 Castrojeriz, Burgos
places.notes: The ruined castle on the hill above town. A steep half-hour climb in the evening gives the best view over the meseta and tomorrow's ridge, Alto de Mostelares.
places.section: Stage 14 · Hornillos del Camino to Castrojeriz · 20 km

places.name: Albergue de Peregrinos San Esteban
places.address: Plaza Mayor 16, 09110 Castrojeriz, Burgos
places.notes: The municipal hostel in an old building on the main square, run on donations. Basic and friendly, in the middle of the long single street of Castrojeriz.
places.section: Stage 14 · Hornillos del Camino to Castrojeriz · 20 km

places.name: Ermita de San Nicolás
places.address: Puente Fitero, 09107 Itero del Castillo, Burgos
places.notes: A 13th-century chapel by the bridge over the Pisuerga, run by an Italian confraternity as a summer-only hostel with no electricity, where hosts wash pilgrims' feet before dinner.
places.section: Stage 15 · Castrojeriz to Frómista · 25 km

places.name: Albergue En El Camino
places.address: Calle Rosario 1, 34468 Boadilla del Camino, Palencia
places.notes: A private hostel with a big lawn, a pool and art on the walls, beside the old stone justice column in Boadilla. A good place to stop short of Frómista.
places.section: Stage 15 · Castrojeriz to Frómista · 25 km

places.name: Iglesia de San Martín de Frómista
places.address: Plaza de San Martín, 34440 Frómista, Palencia
places.notes: A small, almost perfect Romanesque church from the 11th century. Walk around the outside to see more than 300 carved corbels under the eaves.
places.section: Stage 15 · Castrojeriz to Frómista · 25 km

places.name: Iglesia de Santa María la Blanca
places.address: Plaza Mayor, 34449 Villalcázar de Sirga, Palencia
places.notes: A fortress-like Templar church in a tiny village, with painted royal tombs and a Virgin celebrated for miracles in medieval song.
places.section: Stage 16 · Frómista to Carrión de los Condes · 19 km

places.name: Hotel Real Monasterio de San Zoilo
places.address: Calle Obispo Soto Vizoso s/n, 34120 Carrión de los Condes, Palencia
places.notes: A hotel in a Benedictine monastery across the river from Carrión, with a Renaissance cloister open to visitors. A quiet, comfortable splurge on the meseta.
places.section: Stage 16 · Frómista to Carrión de los Condes · 19 km

places.name: Albergue Parroquial de Santa María
places.address: Calle Clérigo Pastor 2, 34120 Carrión de los Condes, Palencia
places.notes: The parish hostel run by the Augustinian sisters, known for an evening of singing and conversation with pilgrims before Mass.
places.section: Stage 16 · Frómista to Carrión de los Condes · 19 km

places.name: Albergue Jacques de Molay
places.address: Calle Iglesia 18, 34349 Terradillos de los Templarios, Palencia
places.notes: A family-run hostel in the village center with dorms, private rooms and a set dinner. Before Calzadilla de la Cueza there is a 17 km stretch with no services, so carry water.
places.section: Stage 17 · Carrión de los Condes to Terradillos de los Templarios · 27 km

places.name: Albergue Los Templarios
places.address: Camino Francés, 34349 Lagartos, Palencia
places.notes: A large brick hostel just before the village, with a lawn, private rooms and a restaurant. The second solid choice in this one-street hamlet.
places.section: Stage 17 · Carrión de los Condes to Terradillos de los Templarios · 27 km

places.name: Arco de San Benito
places.address: Avenida Doctores Bermejo y Calderón, 24320 Sahagún, León
places.notes: A Baroque gate that is nearly all that survives of the once-powerful Benedictine monastery of Sahagún. The brick Mudéjar churches nearby are the town's real character.
places.section: Stage 18 · Terradillos de los Templarios to El Burgo Ranero · 30 km

places.name: Santuario de la Peregrina
places.address: Calle Arco de San Francisco, 24320 Sahagún, León
places.notes: A restored Franciscan convent on the hill, with Mudéjar plasterwork and a museum. Ask here for the certificate marking the halfway point of the Camino.
places.section: Stage 18 · Terradillos de los Templarios to El Burgo Ranero · 30 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal Domenico Laffi
places.address: Calle de la Carretera, 11, 24343 El Burgo Ranero, León
places.notes: A small adobe hostel built in the traditional style, named for a 17th-century Italian pilgrim who wrote about the route. Donation-based and run by volunteers.
places.section: Stage 18 · Terradillos de los Templarios to El Burgo Ranero · 30 km

places.name: Museo de los Pueblos Leoneses
places.address: Calle San Agustín, 24210 Mansilla de las Mulas, León
places.notes: An ethnographic museum in an old Augustinian convent, with costume, farm tools and village crafts from across León province. A good rest stop on an easy day.
places.section: Stage 19 · El Burgo Ranero to Mansilla de las Mulas · 19 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal de Mansilla de las Mulas
places.address: Calle del Puente 5, 24210 Mansilla de las Mulas, León
places.notes: The public hostel inside the medieval walls, with a courtyard full of drying laundry. A short walk from the stretch of town wall above the river.
places.section: Stage 19 · El Burgo Ranero to Mansilla de las Mulas · 19 km

places.name: Catedral de León
places.address: Plaza Regla, 3, 24003 León
places.notes: A Gothic cathedral that is more glass than wall, with nearly 1,800 square meters of medieval stained glass. Visit on a sunny morning when the color falls across the floor.
places.section: Stage 20 · Mansilla de las Mulas to León · 19 km

places.name: Real Colegiata de San Isidoro
places.address: Plaza de San Isidoro 4, 24003 León
places.notes: The Romanesque royal church of León, where the Pantheon of Kings has 12th-century painted vaults in almost perfect condition. Some call it the Sistine Chapel of Romanesque art.
places.section: Stage 20 · Mansilla de las Mulas to León · 19 km

places.name: Albergue de las Benedictinas Santa María de Carbajal
places.address: Plaza de Santa María del Camino 7, 24003 León
places.notes: A convent hostel run by Benedictine nuns in the old town, a few minutes' walk from the cathedral. Pilgrims are invited to the sisters' evening prayer and blessing.
places.section: Stage 20 · Mansilla de las Mulas to León · 19 km

places.name: Parador de León
places.address: Plaza de San Marcos, 7, 24008 León
places.notes: The vast Renaissance convent of San Marcos, once a pilgrim hospital and now a state hotel with a famous plateresque facade. Even if you do not stay, look into the cloister.
places.section: Stage 20 · Mansilla de las Mulas to León · 19 km

places.name: Barrio Húmedo
places.address: Plaza de San Martín, 24003 León
places.notes: The old-town knot of streets around Plaza de San Martín, packed with bars that still serve a free tapa with each drink. Try morcilla and cecina, the cured beef of León.
places.section: Stage 20 · Mansilla de las Mulas to León · 19 km

places.name: Basílica de la Virgen del Camino
places.address: Avenida Astroga, 94, 24198 Virgen Camino, León
places.notes: A striking 1960s sanctuary on the edge of León, with the twelve apostles and the Virgin cast in bronze across its tall front. An unexpected modern church on an old road.
places.section: Stage 21 · León to Hospital de Órbigo · 32 km

places.name: Puente de Órbigo
places.address: Puente de Órbigo, 24286 Hospital de Órbigo, León
places.notes: One of the longest medieval bridges in Spain, about 20 arches, where a knight held a famous jousting challenge in 1434. A tournament is still staged in the fields below each summer.
places.section: Stage 21 · León to Hospital de Órbigo · 32 km

places.name: Albergue Parroquial Karl Leisner
places.address: Calle Álvarez Vega 32, 24286 Hospital de Órbigo, León
places.notes: The parish hostel in an old house with a leafy courtyard, on the main street just past the bridge.
places.section: Stage 21 · León to Hospital de Órbigo · 32 km

places.name: Palacio de Gaudí
places.address: Plaza Eduardo de Castro 15, 24700 Astorga, León
places.notes: A fairytale bishop's palace by Antoni Gaudí, now the Museum of the Ways, with Camino history inside. One of only three Gaudí buildings outside Catalonia.
places.section: Stage 22 · Hospital de Órbigo to Astorga · 17 km

places.name: Albergue Siervas de María
places.address: Plaza de San Francisco 3, 24700 Astorga, León
places.notes: The big association-run hostel at the top of the steep climb into Astorga, right on the route. A terrace with a view toward the Montes de León.
places.section: Stage 22 · Hospital de Órbigo to Astorga · 17 km

places.name: Hostería Cuca la Vaina
places.address: Calle la Magdalena, 10, 24718 Castrillo de los Polvazares, León
places.notes: A short detour to a stone village built by muleteers, where this inn serves cocido maragato, a stew eaten backward, meats first and soup last. Plan on a big lunch and a short afternoon.
places.section: Stage 23 · Astorga to Rabanal del Camino · 20 km

places.name: Refugio Gaucelmo
places.address: Lugar Rabanal Camino, 21D, 24722 Santa Colomba de Somoza, León
places.notes: A volunteer-run hostel in a restored priest's house with a walled garden, set up by the UK-based Confraternity of Saint James. Open April to October, with afternoon tea and the monks' sung prayers at the church next door.
places.section: Stage 23 · Astorga to Rabanal del Camino · 20 km

places.name: Cruz de Ferro
places.address: LE-142, 24722 Santa Colomba de Somoza, León
places.notes: A small iron cross on a tall wooden pole near the highest point of the Camino, on a mound of stones carried by pilgrims from home. Bring one and leave it with whatever it stands for.
places.section: Stage 24 · Rabanal del Camino to Molinaseca · 25 km

places.name: Puente de los Peregrinos
places.address: Calle Real, 24413 Molinaseca, León
places.notes: A medieval bridge over the Meruelo into Molinaseca, with a river pool below where tired walkers soak after the long descent from the mountains.
places.section: Stage 24 · Rabanal del Camino to Molinaseca · 25 km

places.name: Hostal El Palacio
places.address: Calle El Palacio 19, 24413 Molinaseca, León
places.notes: A small family hostal at the end of the bridge, with a terrace restaurant over the river. Private rooms for a night off from bunks.
places.section: Stage 24 · Rabanal del Camino to Molinaseca · 25 km

places.name: Castillo de los Templarios
places.address: Avenida del Castillo, 131–143, 24401 Ponferrada, León
places.notes: A great Templar castle in the middle of Ponferrada, with towers, walls and a library of facsimile medieval books inside. Give it an hour on the way through.
places.section: Stage 25 · Molinaseca to Villafranca del Bierzo · 31 km

places.name: Iglesia de Santiago
places.address: Calle Santiago, 24500 Villafranca del Bierzo, León
places.notes: A Romanesque church with the Puerta del Perdón, where sick medieval pilgrims who could go no farther could receive the same pardon as at Santiago.
places.section: Stage 25 · Molinaseca to Villafranca del Bierzo · 31 km

places.name: Albergue Ave Fénix
places.address: Calle Santiago 10, 24500 Villafranca del Bierzo, León
places.notes: A long-running private hostel beside the church of Santiago, built and rebuilt by the Jato family. Rustic, with a communal dinner and a lot of Camino history.
places.section: Stage 25 · Molinaseca to Villafranca del Bierzo · 31 km

places.name: Santuario de Santa María a Real do Cebreiro
places.address: O Cebreiro, 27671 Pedrafita do Cebreiro, Lugo
places.notes: One of the oldest churches on the Camino, pre-Romanesque in origin, with the chalice of a medieval Eucharistic miracle. The parish priest here painted the first yellow arrows.
places.section: Stage 26 · Villafranca del Bierzo to O Cebreiro · 28 km

places.name: Albergue de Peregrinos do Cebreiro
places.address: Lugar Cebreiro, 17, 27671 Pedrafita do Cebreiro, Lugo
places.notes: The Xunta's public hostel at the top of the village, with views over the Galician hills on a clear evening. Popular, so arrive early in season.
places.section: Stage 26 · Villafranca del Bierzo to O Cebreiro · 28 km

places.name: Conxunto Etnográfico do Cebreiro
places.address: O Cebreiro, 27671 Pedrafita do Cebreiro, Lugo
places.notes: Round stone houses with thatched roofs, a style of mountain dwelling older than the Romans. One palloza is kept as a small museum of village life.
places.section: Stage 26 · Villafranca del Bierzo to O Cebreiro · 28 km

places.name: Monumento ao Peregrino
places.address: LU-633, Alto de San Roque, 27671 Pedrafita do Cebreiro, Lugo
places.notes: A large bronze pilgrim leaning into the wind, hat clamped down, at a pass about 4 km past O Cebreiro. The best photo stop of the morning.
places.section: Stage 27 · O Cebreiro to Triacastela · 21 km

places.name: Albergue de Peregrinos de Triacastela
places.address: Rúa do Peregrino, 27630 Triacastela, Lugo
places.notes: The Xunta hostel in a meadow at the entrance to the village after the long descent. Triacastela's cafés and its pilgrim menus are a short walk away.
places.section: Stage 27 · O Cebreiro to Triacastela · 21 km

places.name: Mosteiro de Samos
places.address: Rúa Compostela, 27620 Samos, Lugo
places.notes: One of the oldest monasteries in Spain, still home to Benedictine monks, at the bottom of a green river valley. Take the Samos route out of Triacastela for this; the monks lead guided visits.
places.section: Stage 28 · Triacastela to Sarria via Samos · 25 km

places.name: Albergue de Peregrinos de Sarria
places.address: Rúa Maior 79, 27600 Sarria, Lugo
places.notes: The Xunta hostel on the old main street up the hill. Sarria is the start for many walkers aiming for the last 100 km, so the trail gets busier from here.
places.section: Stage 28 · Triacastela to Sarria via Samos · 25 km

places.name: Igrexa de San Nicolás de Portomarín
places.address: Plaza Conde Fenosa, 27170 Portomarín, Lugo
places.notes: A fortified Romanesque church moved stone by stone up the hill in the 1960s when the old town was flooded for a reservoir. The numbers on the stones are still visible.
places.section: Stage 29 · Sarria to Portomarín · 22 km

places.name: Albergue de Peregrinos de Portomarín
places.address: Rúa Fraga Iribarne, 27170 Portomarín, Lugo
places.notes: The public hostel in the upper town near the church. Cross the long bridge over the Miño reservoir and climb the stairs to reach it.
places.section: Stage 29 · Sarria to Portomarín · 22 km

places.name: Castro de Castromaior
places.address: LU-633, Castromaior, 27188 Portomarín, Lugo
places.notes: An Iron Age hill fort beside the trail with the stone footings of round houses inside its rings of walls. Free to wander, and almost no one stops.
places.section: Stage 30 · Portomarín to Palas de Rei · 25 km

places.name: Albergue de Peregrinos de Palas de Rei
places.address: Avenida de Compostela 19, 27200 Palas de Rei, Lugo
places.notes: The Xunta hostel on the main road in the middle of town, close to cafés and shops.
places.section: Stage 30 · Portomarín to Palas de Rei · 25 km

places.name: Pulpería Ezequiel
places.address: Avenida de Lugo, 15800 Melide, A Coruña
places.notes: Melide is the octopus town of the Camino, and this long hall of shared tables is the classic stop for pulpo á feira on wooden plates with bread and young white wine.
places.section: Stage 31 · Palas de Rei to Arzúa · 29 km

places.name: Albergue Municipal de Arzúa
places.address: Rúa Cima do Lugar 6, 15810 Arzúa, A Coruña
places.notes: The Xunta hostel in an old stone building on the main square of Arzúa. Pick up some of the local soft cheese for tomorrow's lunch.
places.section: Stage 31 · Palas de Rei to Arzúa · 29 km

places.name: Albergue de Peregrinos de Arca do Pino
places.address: Avenida de Lugo 30, 15821 O Pedrouzo, A Coruña
places.notes: The Xunta hostel on the main road through O Pedrouzo, the last night for most pilgrims before Santiago.
places.section: Stage 32 · Arzúa to O Pedrouzo · 19 km

places.name: Igrexa de Santa Eulalia de Arca
places.address: A Igrexa, Arca, 15821 O Pino, A Coruña
places.notes: The parish church of Arca, just off the main road through O Pedrouzo. Many pilgrims go to the evening Mass here on their last night before Santiago.
places.section: Stage 32 · Arzúa to O Pedrouzo · 19 km

places.name: Monte do Gozo
places.address: Monte do Gozo, 15892 Santiago de Compostela, A Coruña
places.notes: The hill where pilgrims got their first view of the cathedral spires, marked by a monument for the 1989 papal visit and statues of two pilgrims pointing west. About 5 km to go.
places.section: Stage 33 · O Pedrouzo to Santiago de Compostela · 20 km

places.name: Catedral de Santiago de Compostela
places.address: Praza do Obradoiro, 15704 Santiago de Compostela, A Coruña
places.notes: The end of the road: the Portico of Glory, the tomb of Saint James and the hug of the apostle's statue behind the altar. Check the official site for the pilgrim Mass and when the botafumeiro swings.
places.section: Stage 33 · O Pedrouzo to Santiago de Compostela · 20 km

places.name: Oficina del Peregrino
places.address: Rúa das Carretas 33, 15705 Santiago de Compostela, A Coruña
places.notes: Where pilgrims who have walked at least the last 100 km with a stamped credential receive the Compostela. Register online before you arrive to skip much of the line.
places.section: Stage 33 · O Pedrouzo to Santiago de Compostela · 20 km

places.name: Parador Hostal dos Reis Católicos
places.address: Rúa Obradoiro, 1, 15707 Santiago de Compostela, A Coruña, España
places.notes: A royal pilgrim hospital from 1499 on the cathedral square, now a state hotel with four cloisters. A traditional splurge for the last night.
places.section: Stage 33 · O Pedrouzo to Santiago de Compostela · 20 km

places.name: Albergue Seminario Menor
places.address: Avenida de Quiroga Palacios 2, 15703 Santiago de Compostela, A Coruña
places.notes: A huge former seminary turned hostel on a hill above the old town, with dorms and simple private rooms. A good base for a couple of days in the city.
places.section: Stage 33 · O Pedrouzo to Santiago de Compostela · 20 km

places.name: Mercado de Abastos
places.address: Rúa das Ameas s/n, 15704 Santiago de Compostela, A Coruña
places.notes: Santiago's stone food market, with fish, shellfish, cheese and produce from Galician farms. Some stalls will cook what you buy at a counter nearby.
places.section: Stage 33 · O Pedrouzo to Santiago de Compostela · 20 km
